_comment: Central product registry (source of truth) - your plans live here. Every offering = ONE Digistore24 product PER LANGUAGE, and every WAY TO PAY for it = one payment plan on that product. Monthly and yearly are two entries in 'paymentOptions', NOT two products and not two Product Keys: both buyers hold the same key and the same entitlement, so hasPlan() asks one question and a planKeys list names one key. This list is deliberately hard-coded: reshape it or delete what you do not need. It feeds BOTH the plans page (/plans) and the sync script (scripts/ds24/sync-products.mjs), which creates the products at Digistore24 and writes the ids back into 'productIds.<env>' and 'payplanIds.<env>.<lang>.<option>'. The PRICE is AUTHORED here and nowhere else - the sync copies it onto the payment plans, because our checkout link is not the only way into the product (its own order form, an affiliate link and the buyer's own interval switch all charge what hangs on the product). Do not edit those plans in the Digistore24 interface: the next sync overwrites them from this file. The keys below ('basic', 'starter') are identifiers, not display text. Rename them only before your first live sale.
_languageComment: Each environment set in productIds is one Digistore24 product per language, and it is not a convenience — a DS24 product carries exactly ONE language, and that language is the language of the ORDER FORM the buyer fills in (field labels, buttons, payment methods, cancellation terms). createBuyUrl has no parameter to override it. So an app whose UI speaks four languages needs FOUR products per offering, one per locale. Cover every locale from i18n/config.ts here; a locale with no entry still sells, but its buyers land on another language's form ('node run.mjs ds24-sync' warns about the gap). The language also decides the marketplace the approval is requested from: German -> Digistore24 Germany (siteowner 1), everything else -> USA (2). Your product COPY ('name', 'description', 'tagline', 'features') is deliberately NOT translated — it is your text, and the same one is sent to every language product.
_envComment: 'productIds' holds ONE PRODUCT SET PER ENVIRONMENT (dev/staging/prod): 'node run.mjs ds24-sync --env <env>' maintains exactly one of them and never touches the others. The dev/staging products carry a visible ' [DEV]'/' [STAGING]' suffix in their name; prod names stay clean. Staging is optional — most apps go dev -> prod, which is fine as long as they test. 'syncId' is this app's own identity inside the vendor's account: it is written into every product's internal note and is what 'ds24-sync --prune' reads before it deletes or deactivates anything - never regenerate it, or every product this app created stops looking like ours. 'productGroupId' is the ONE Digistore24 product group (folder) of this app, shared by every environment; the sync creates it once and keeps every product in it. Both are written back by the sync — treat them like the product ids: committed, never hand-edited.
_billingModeComment: What this app sells: 'subscriptions' (plans only), 'tokens' (prepaid credit only) or 'both'. ONE switch — it turns off the surfaces of the model you do not use (a balance card stuck at 0, an empty 'next payment' card), so you do not have to hunt them down page by page. It is COSMETIC: hasPlan(), consumeTokens() and the IPN behave the same in every mode, and a mode only ever hides an EMPTY card — a customer who still holds tokens keeps seeing them after a switch. Set it, then delete the products below that you do not sell; lib/billing-mode.test.ts fails the build if the two contradict each other. Details: lib/billing-mode.ts.
_sellComment: "sell" is the switch between "I offer this" and "this is a template I keep". A missing field means SOLD, so every registry written before this field existed keeps selling; only a literal false parks an entry. A parked entry stays in this file as a shape to copy from, but "node run.mjs ds24-sync" creates no Digistore24 product for it and /plans does not show it — that is the difference from deleting it. PARKING IS ABOUT SELLING, NEVER ABOUT ACCESS: whoever already bought it keeps it, hasPlan() still answers for it, and its refunds and cancellations keep arriving. It also does not unpublish anything: a product that was synced while it was on sale stays buyable at Digistore24 through an old checkout link until you deactivate it THERE, by hand — the sync says so when it meets one. Creating products is the step that cannot be undone from here, so ds24-sync refuses to create NEW ones until you have seen the list and re-run it with --create-new. Parking is still not the same as removing: a product that is genuinely no longer wanted is taken out of this file, and the next 'node run.mjs ds24-sync --prune' deletes it at Digistore24 - or deactivates it, if it ever sold anything.
